recipes.name: Southwest Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green chile peppers
1 (15 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained
1 (8.75 ounce) can whole kernel corn, drained

steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts and sear for 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Add tomatoes with green chiles, black beans, and corn. Reduce heat and let simmer until chicken is cooked through and the juices run clear, 25 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Southwest Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Healthy and hearty, chicken simmers with tomatoes, black beans and corn.

video.description: See how to make a hearty Southwest-style chicken with black beans, corn, tomatoes, and diced green chile peppers. It’s the best of all possible worlds: healthy, quick, and delicious—a great weeknight alternative.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is GREAT! I did make a few changes: I diced up some onion and garlic and sautéed it in the oil. Then I cut the chicken breasts into bite size pieces and sprinkled some hot chili powder on the chicken pieces prior to browning. I then added the tomatoes with green chili peppers, beans and I used frozen corn and it turned out fantastic. I did try to freeze it and it freezes really good. However, I would suggest if you do freeze it you may want to add the beans in closer to the end of the cooking time because mine were a little soft after reheating. GREAT DISH!!!

I made this. I used rotisserie chicken and taco seasoning. I cooked rice with water and juice of one lime and cilantro and added it to chicken with onions beans corn and Rotel tomatoes with peppers and taco seasoning. I have used it in a burrito with all the fixings. It is a wonderful thing!

I too seasoned (red pepper, ancho chili powder, tiny bit of seasoned salt) and browned the chicken, removed it from the pan, & added some minced onion and garlic to simmer in the oil until fragrant. Meanwhile I sliced the chicken and added it back into the pot. I used fire roasted tomatoes and a 4 oz can of green chilies instead. I used two chicken breasts as I’m cooking for two, so I halved the corn and black beans and let it simmer adding a bit of cornstarch so the sauce would thicken. I then served it over jasmine rice. Last minute and delicious!

A few changes and note my 5-star why

1) I preseasoned my chicken with Goya Adobo with cumin, a little fresh cumin, some garlic powder, some onion powder, cayenne powder and a little Mrs. Dash - Table Blend. 

2) I used jasmine rice in lieu of regular while rice. Very aromatic and flavorful. 

3. In the sauté process, 1/4 of one vidillia onion and two teaspoons of garlic paste was added, along with a little more Adobo and fresh cumin. 

4) I also substituted finely diced tomatos with garlic and olive oil, a can of Goya black bean soup and a bag of Birds-Eye gold and white corn (I precooked this before adding). 

5) I cooked the chicken to about 85% done (minimal pink remaining), added the remaining ingredients then simmered for 40 minutes. 

This is magnificent.

Tasty! My hubs and I liked this quite a bit, albeit with a bit of doctoring on my part. :) I felt this would be pretty bleh as written, so to add a little pizzaz, I seasoned my chicken (which I cubed) with 1/4 teaspoon each of chipotle chili powder, cumin and salt. I also sautéed a small chopped onion and minced garlic clove in a little EVOO BEFORE browning my chicken. I then proceeded as directed. Because I was only serving two adults, I halved everything (which was easy to do since I already had a half can of beans in my fridge and was measuring the corn from a bag in my freezer). Serving this over brown rice with cubed avocado, a dollop of sour cream and fresh lime was a fantastic (and yummy!) idea. Thanks for sharing your healthy recipe, Tamcattt. With a little tweaking, this wasn't bland in the least! :-)

My family enjoyed this recipe! I did cut the chicken into cubes prior to cooking simply to make it easier for my kids to eat. I also added two cloves of minced garlic and some taco seasoning. It gave it a nice flavor. I served it over rice to round it out as a complete meal.
I cubed the chicken and seasoned it with garlic, onion, cumin and smoked paprika before sauteing. I also used a can of seasoned beans (undrained). This went over really well with family.

Took the recommendations of the others by adding garlic, onions, chili powder, and I added a bit of salt, pepper, and cayenne pepper too, and OH it was Delicious! I put my portion on a bed of romaine with Tomatillo (green) Salsa as the dressing and it was perfect! My husband and step-daughter love cheese, so after I took my portion out of the cast iron skillet, I sprinkled on some shredded cheese and covered it for a few extra minutes so it could melt. Saving this to make again!

I put this together ahead of time for a busy night, so I made a few changes. I drizzled olive oil in a baking pan, put chicken breast tenders in the pan, sprinkled with salt, pepper and cumin, topped with salsa, corn and beans. Baked at 350 for 30 min covered, then removed foil to evaporate some juice. The family loved it, chicken was juicy and tender.

Like others, I cut up the chicken and seasoned it w/chili, onion, and garlic powders along w/cumin and some oregano. I also sautéed some diced onion and garlic in olive oil prior to adding the chicken. I used seasoned black beans, too. It turned out great. There was more liquid than I expected but using a slotted serving spoon to serve over rice made the dish a hit. I also added some Mexican cheese mix at serving time. It was great and will definitely keep it as part of my dinner rotation.
I work two jobs and really don’t have time to cook so I prep my meals. This was awesome giving me at least four or five nights of meals.
Lots of flavor! I added some Hatch chili peppers I had on hand, then topped it all with Mexican blend cheese & served over rice.
I tend to avoid recipes requiring so many tweaks. Lesson learned.
Yes, I added a chopped onion, garlic powder and a dash of worchestersire. I small oxo cube. Also 1 tsp. of chili flakes. Served over hot rice! Great . I’ll make it again ✅
As written, this is a mess. That the top rated review is practically its own, different recipe should tell you something.

As written, this recipe is bland and boring. Yes, it can be fixed with some adjustments, but rating the recipe itself, it's a dud. Read through the reviews to find the tweaks that sound good to you, and follow your gut. Onion and garlic is a must though.

This recipe was really good with a bit of tweaks. I added garlic, onion, and chili powder. I also added coriander, slap your mama, and ground pepper. I added green, orange and red bell peppers. Finally I added chicken broth and served it with jasmine rice. Winner winner chicken dinner.
This was rather bland like others have said. I did shred the chicken and make them into wraps. I used cojita cheese and a little taco seasoning to help.
Very new and wonderful tasting meal!! I love the black beans in it!! My do , which is an Italian Greyhoind just loves it, herself!! Id highly recommend this one!! Yum!! Tane Clark
